seen.extent: HMC: eight pages of cipher (Bennet to Fanshaw, 6 Oct 1664; original not seen); the printed letter of 25 Aug 1664 viewed at p. 283 of the 1701 edition
seen.cipher: Page 283 of the 1701 Original Letters prints 'Whitehal, August 25. 1664' to Ambassador Fanshaw with parts of the text set in italics (e.g. 'It is his Majesties Pleasure...'), the printer's convention for passages that were in cipher in the original. HMC says the eight cipher pages 'prove to be the cipher part of the letter dated August 25th in the printed letters (p. 283)' and that the key is among the papers. So a decipherment is in print.

prior_art.decode: Not on DECODE: known.py (Heathcote, Fanshawe, Bennet) found only leads 988/989, the IA candidate files and CATALOGUE.md's sweep note.
prior_art.tomokiyo: Cryptiana 'King Charles II's Ciphers during Exile' cites the Heathcote MSS only for Charles II's 1649 letter in Fanshaw's own cipher; nothing on the 1664 Bennet-Fanshaw cipher.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry or HistoCrypt item on Bennet-Fanshaw 1664 found in two web searches.
prior_art.edition: Original Letters of Sir Richard Fanshaw (1701, A. Roper), p. 283: Bennet to Fanshaw, 25 Aug 1664, with italicised (deciphered) passages; HMC Heathcote 1899 states the identity.
prior_art.literature: HMC Heathcote 1899 (Lomas) is the only description; a web search for where the Heathcote papers are now found only the HMC calendar and Fanshawe family collection records, not the MS.

989.key_check: The key is stated by HMC to be among the Heathcote papers (not held here, not online); none needed, because the plaintext is printed in the 1701 edition and gives the cipher part of the 6 Oct 1664 packet.
989.duplicates: known.py 'Heathcote' 'Fanshawe' 'Bennet': only leads 988/989 and CATALOGUE.md sweep text; no catalogue or DECODE twin. Lead 988 is a different packet.
989.closed: HMC says the eight cipher pages are the cipher part of the letter printed in 1701 at p. 283; I viewed that page and it carries italicised deciphered passages, so a reading existed in print; the original sheets are not online and were not compared line by line.

988.unvetted: Same Heathcote packet type as 989, but HMC says the six pages (13 Jun 1664) are a duplicate of cipher parts of letters of 8 Apr, 12 May and 2 Jun re-enciphered in Coventry's cipher. I viewed the 1701 print of Bennet's 7 Apr 1664 letter (p. 56): no italics on its first page; I did not check the 12 May and 2 Jun letters for italicised deciphered passages, and the original is not online. Needs that check before a verdict.
